items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: People, when I say Kansas City, they say: Oh you know … because so many famous jazz musicians particularly have come from Kansas City, that area … and they hear the name Henderson … and Fletcher Henderson and Horace Henderson … I would say that there's a possibility that we may have been, let’s say sprung from the same plantation. My sister at one time did a … research on the family and I think she came up

with the fact that we had, that my grand, my great grandfather, or somebody like that in that area were slaves on a plantation owned by the Hendersohns, s-o-h-n, who were Dutch people, and that they were, if you can think of such, I guess, benevolent slaves owners in a way of speaking because they freed their slaves. Something like that. I don't know the specific details. At any rate, that’s how come Kansas City and Oklahoma, as I said, we lived in Watonga. I remember that because my mother used to show me these…
